title: Methods for traceable scanning magnetometry using single nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond: determining orientation, distance and localization
authors: Nikhita Khera, Ephraim Spindler, Yanis Abdedou, Marcel Gasser, Sandra Wolff, Bert Lägel, Robert Frömter, Mathias Weiler, Mathias Kläui, Elke Neu
abstract: Individual, scannable nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in single crystal diamond nanostructures enable nanoscale, quantitative imaging of magnetic stray fields. Nevertheless, important parameters like distance between the NV center and the sample and the orientation of the NV high symmetry axis are often not known precisely and enter data evaluation as free fitting parameters. We here use scanning NV imaging on micro-patterned, perpendicularly magnetized stripes and discs. From these measurements, we directly infer NV - sample distance d_NV and the NV's azimuthal orientation without the need for an external vector magnet control. We determine d_NV = 31.5 nm, while we infer the azimuthal orientation with a precision of 3°. We additionally employ commercially available silicon needles to image the apex topography of our diamond nanostructures to detect surface contamination. Simultaneously, monitoring NV fluorescence as a function of the needle's position allows us to estimate the lateral placement of the NV inside the diamond nanostructure.
summary: This work presents advanced techniques for using single NV centers in diamond to map magnetic fields at the nanoscale. By analyzing stray fields from patterned magnetic films (stripes and discs), the authors developed a robust calibration method that determines crucial unknown parameters like the probe distance ($d_{NV}$) and NV orientation ($\phi$). This significantly enhances the quantitative capability of SNVM for fundamental studies in condensed matter magnetism.
main_problem: The primary goal is to enable nanoscale, quantitative imaging of magnetic stray fields using single Nitrogen Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond by accurately determining unknown parameters like the NV-sample distance and its orientation.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a method to directly infer the NV center's standoff distance ($d_{NV} = 31.5 	ext{ nm}$) and its azimuthal orientation ($\phi$) with high precision, all without requiring external vector magnet control.
method: A multi-step calibration protocol is employed using patterned magnetic samples (PMA stripes and discs) to map the NV fluorescence signal, which is sensitive to the local magnetic field projected onto the NV axis.
model_or_system: The system uses a single NV center in a diamond nanopillar probe scanning over perpendicularly magnetized thin films. The measurement relies on modeling the stray magnetic field ($\mathbf{B}$) from these patterned samples using analytic expressions involving complete elliptic integrals for discs, and simpler forms for stripes.
key_observables: NV fluorescence signal (Zeeman shift), which is proportional to $	ext{BNV} = \mathbf{n}_{NV} \cdot \mathbf{B}$.
important_parameters: $d_{NV}$ (standoff distance), $\phi$ (azimuthal orientation), and the magnetic magnetization ($M_{st}$) of the sample.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include negligible thickness for discs ($t \ll d_{NV}$) and that the measured field is solely generated by the patterned sample structure, allowing calibration to remove unknown geometric factors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of NV placement over PMA stripes and discs, showing how stray fields encode $\phi$. Other figures show SEM/AFM images of these patterns and fluorescence dip analysis from inverse AFM measurements.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need to calibrate unknown parameters ($d_{NV}, \phi$) in SNVM. It details a three-step calibration protocol: using stripe line-cuts for $d_{NV}$, then using disc maps to find $\phi$, and finally employing inverse AFM measurements on silicon needles to map lateral NV placement.
why_interesting: While the core technique is magnetometry, the ability to precisely characterize geometric parameters ($d_{NV}, \phi$) *in situ* without external controls makes this a powerful tool for quantum sensing platforms, relevant to understanding coupling strengths in solid-state qubits.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) center geometry and sensing principles. (a) Unit cell of the diamond lattice highlighting the NV center orientation. The Nitrogen (N) and Vacancy (V) define the high symmetry axis nNV, forming a polar angle θ with respect to the surface normal, ns along the z-axis. (b) Schematic of the scanning NV microscopy setup. The NV-containing diamond nanopillar probe is scanned close to the sample surface. The NV has a stand-off distance dNV above the sample surface. The magnetic field projection depends on both the polar angle θ and the azimuthal angle ϕ. (c) The energy level diagram of the NV (left) and the Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (ODMR) spectrum...

Figure 2: (a) Schematic illustrating the NV center in the probe, at a stand-off distance dNV above the stripe edge. The out of plane magnetization Ms, produces a stray field along the edge. (b) Schematic of the scanning NV nanopillar probe above a PMA disc, shown in side view (left) and top view (right). The out-of-plane magnetization M produces a radial stray field at the disc edge (arrows). The angular position of the field extremum along the edge (highlighted arc) encodes the azimuth ϕ of the NV axis, measured from the +x axis.
Figure 3: (a) SEM image (main) and AFM topog- raphy (inset) of the PMA stripe. (b) SEM image (main) and AFM topography (inset) of the PMA disc
Figure 4: Two-dimensional BNV map over the stripe region. The map shows the stray magnetic field BNV measured over the edge of a PMA stripe. The color scale indicates BNV in mT.

Figure 5: NV-to-sample distance calibration from stripe edge line scans. (a) Representative BNV line scan (blue points) acquired perpendicular to the stripe edge, together with the fitted stray-field model (red curve). (b) Summary of dNV (top) and Ms (bottom) values extracted from ten independent line scans distributed along the stripe edge. The solid lines and shaded bands indicate the mean and the ±1σ standard deviation across the ensemble, respec- tively.

NV sensing of materials.note: This paper directly describes advanced techniques for using single NV centers in diamond (SNVM) to map magnetic fields from patterned samples, which is central to the scope of quantum relaxometry and scanning NV magnetometry.
